Definition: to be frail, feeble, or (figuratively) melancholy
BiblicalUsage: The word means frail, feeble, sick past healing: the child of David and Bathsheba was struck and was very sick; Jeremiah says the heart is deceitful above all things and desperately wicked, past knowing; and twice the wound is called incurable — thy bruise is incurable, thy wound is grievous, and her wound is incurable, for it has come unto Judah. The word is used for a dying child, a deceitful heart, and a wound no physician can heal.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe this word is the Bible's honest diagnosis: the heart is desperately wicked, and the wound is incurable — no man can heal it and no effort can fix it. That is why the gospel has to be a new heart and not a repaired one, and why I hold that only God can do what Jeremiah says no one can: know the heart, and heal the wound that is past healing.
